Wir suchen Menschen, die experimentieren, ohne auf Erlaubnis zu warten, KI über das Offensichtliche hinaus nutzen und wissen, wann man ihr vertrauen kann - und wann man sie hinterfragen sollte. 

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Join us as an Anti-Financial Crime Working Student or Intern to improve the operational processes behind Qonto’s German branch. You’ll join our Central Europe AFC team and begin with a high-impact challenge: making sure sensitive physical correspondence—including court documents, legal notices, seizures, and law-enforcement requests—is received, routed, tracked, and handled on time. As you gain autonomy, you’ll connect teams across AFC, Banking Operations, Legal, and Product while helping us build clearer and more reliable ways of working.

➡️ As an Anti-Financial Crime Working Student or Intern at Qonto, you will:
  • Improve a critical operational process: Map our current physical-mail workflow, understand how documents move from our external provider to internal teams, and identify unclear ownership, bottlenecks, and missed handoffs.
  • Build a reliable coordination system: Help design and maintain clear routing rules, trackers, ownership models, escalation paths, and follow-up routines so sensitive requests reach the right people on time.
  • Connect teams across Qonto: Coordinate with AFC, AML, Fraud, Banking Operations, Legal, and other stakeholders to gather information, clarify responsibilities, and maintain visibility on open actions.
  • Support AFC and Product projects: Once the core workflow is stable, help organize our Product × AFC feature-approval process, including coordinating input from multiple MLROs across Europe.
  • Improve how we work with AI: Experiment with AI to structure information, document workflows, prepare updates, and reduce repetitive coordination work—while checking outputs carefully and protecting sensitive information.


 ➡️ What you can expect:
  • A concrete project with visible impact: Your first mission addresses an important operational risk for Qonto’s German branch. Your work will contribute directly to the timely handling of sensitive banking and legal procedures.
  • Broad exposure across Qonto: You’ll work beyond a single team and gain insight into AFC, operations, legal, product, growth, and marketing within Germany—Qonto’s second-largest branch.
  • Real ownership: This is project-based work rather than a list of repetitive daily tasks. You’ll be expected to investigate problems, propose practical solutions, and turn them into sustainable processes.
  • Progressive scope: You’ll begin with the physical-mail workflow. As you establish a reliable process, you’ll take on additional coordination projects across AFC and Product.
  • Hybrid work in Berlin: Approximately 3 days per week in the office to support learning and collaboration.


 ➡️ About You:
  • You are an enrolled student: You may be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Law, Economics, Marketing, or another relevant field. We are open to different academic backgrounds and do not require a specific specialization.
  • You are autonomous and accountable: You can take a loosely defined problem, ask the right questions, structure your approach, and make concrete progress without waiting for step-by-step instructions.
  • You are organized and rigorous: You can track several stakeholders, owners, deadlines, and dependencies while understanding why small gaps matter when legal or regulatory requests are involved.
  • You learn quickly: Previous AFC or banking experience is not required, but you are curious about financial crime, banking operations, legal processes, and how a fintech works.
  • You are comfortable with digital tools: You can work confidently with Google Workspace. Familiarity with Notion is particularly useful.
  • You have professional English: English is the team’s working language. German is a plus, but it is not mandatory; Dutch is an additional bonus.
  • You are curious about AI: You are willing to experiment with AI to organize information and improve processes while maintaining accuracy, judgment, and confidentiality.


About your future Manager:
You manager will be Stefano, Anti-Financial Crime Director for Central Europe and Oversight and Deputy Managing Director for Germany. He’ll give you the context and support needed to understand sensitive AFC and banking processes while trusting you to investigate problems, propose solutions, and progressively take ownership.

  • His background? Stefano joined Qonto in 2025 after nearly a decade in AML and compliance roles across banking and crypto, including Senior Manager for Risk & Compliance at PwC, AML and Compliance Officer at Coinbase Germany and Upvest, and earlier compliance positions at Intesa Sanpaolo and Deutsche Bank. At Qonto, he oversees Anti-Financial Crime topics across Central Europe and contributes to the governance of the German branch.
  • What he brings to the team? A combination of regulatory perspective, cross-market experience, and an autonomous management style. Stefano does not micromanage: he creates space to test ideas and solve problems independently while remaining available for daily guidance, brainstorming, and regular project checkpoints.

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
This role starts on the content platform, and the platform surface it serves is growing. The foundations of the company, identity and access, developer platform, data and the infrastructure everything runs on, are being invested in over the coming year. We are looking for someone whose curiosity does not stop at the edge of their own team, because the interesting problems here sit exactly where those layers meet. 

There is genuine ambiguity in this space right now, and a decision or two you would inherit that we have not finished making. We would rather tell you that than have you discover it in month two. The upside is that very little here is set, so the person who takes this shapes the layer everything else in the product is built on for the next several years. 

Requirements

  • Own the content services every surface depends on. The services and APIs that serve content to the learner surface, the admin surface and everything we build next, plus the delivery path including CDN and video, and file and asset storage. 
  • Own the structural contract. How content is stored, versioned and served so it can be reused and assembled differently for different customers. This is a schema and interface problem before it is a tooling problem, and your measure is whether the contract other teams build against is clear, stable and safe to change. 
  • Own multi tenant separation. Making sure one customer’s content and branding stay theirs. The tenancy model needs a decision and an owner, and that will be one of your first real pieces of work. 
  • Own access, entitlements and data residency. Who can reach what, where data lives, and what we are able to commit to contractually. 
  • Own performance and cost per tenant. If this layer is slow, everything is slow. If it is expensive, it is expensive everywhere. 
  • Carry the platform half of a migration already in flight. We are moving off an incumbent content tool while the current system keeps earning. Sequencing that is the real work, and the order matters more than the ambition. 
  • Own the non functional questions that show up in deals. A meaningful share of our deals slow down in security and compliance review rather than in the pitch, and that is a product problem with a revenue number attached. 

This role is for you if you have:

  • Experience with content management as a product, whether that is a CMS, a DAM, a headless content platform or a structured content system at scale. This is our primary preference. 
  • Experience owning platform or infrastructure adjacent product, where success was measured in what other teams could build rather than in features a customer names. 
  • Enough technical depth to be useful and the honesty to say where you are not. You can read an architecture proposal, ask the question that unpicks it, and tell the difference between a researched answer and a fluent one. 
  • The ability to hold your own with senior engineers, infrastructure engineers and security specialists. Not as a peer on implementation, but well enough that a remediation estimate or a tenancy design does not go unchallenged. A previous career as an engineer is a real advantage and not a requirement. 
  • A habit of thinking in seams. Where systems meet, what a contract between them should guarantee, and how to keep a decision reversible rather than walking through a one way door. 
  • The ability to sequence. We are modernising a platform that carries real history while it keeps earning, and the order matters more than the ambition. 
  • Writing. Decisions, tradeoffs and the reasoning behind them, in a way an engineer and an executive can both act on. 
  • Nice to have, and genuinely useful: depth in AI and personalisation, or in infrastructure. Either one compounds with this role, and we are not expecting both. 

This role is not for you if:

  • You want to be a delivery manager for the engineers. They are strong and they do not need coordinating. They need decisions and clarity about what matters. 
  • You want to own the authoring and editorial experience itself. A colleague owns that, you will work closely with them, and drawing the seam between you well is part of the job. 
  • You want to run a rewrite programme. Foundations serve outcomes, and a foundation with no customer outcome attached does not get funded here and should not. 
  • You need the surrounding decisions settled before you arrive.

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
We are growing this team while it delivers, on a platform with real history, and some of what we currently believe will turn out to be wrong. The incumbent HR suites are consolidating and buying their way into this space, so the clock is real. 

The problem underneath it is genuinely unsolved. Nobody has built software that knows what a person needs to be able to do next week, teaches it in the few minutes they actually have, and observes whether it landed without asking them. Not the language apps, which have the habit but not the stakes. Not the platforms, which have the content but not the attention. Not the HR suites, which have the data but have never made anything a person voluntarily opens. 

If that sounds like a problem worth several years, we should talk. 

As our Senior Product Manager for the learner experience, you own the surface where learning actually happens, for the person actually doing it. It is the most visible product role in the company, because everything else in our strategy depends on somebody coming back on a Tuesday. Today weekly active learners sits close to one percent. That number is the job. 

Requirements

  • Own the learner surface end to end. Onboarding, what someone is offered next, how it arrives, and what we learn from what they did. 
  • Move us from a catalogue people browse to a product that pays attention. Personalisation here is a spectrum, not a feature: country and industry, company size, whether they reach us through their own LMS or directly, then company, department, team and finally the individual. A fifteen minute bus ride should be able to become seven minutes of audio and three quick questions, assembled for that person. 
  • Partner with our educational designers on how it reaches one person. They have decades of research behind how our content is built, in activities of two to eight minutes designed for habit formation. What is not yet settled is how those pieces compose into a path for one person, and you would be one of the people settling it. Your half is the one they cannot do on their own: how it reaches one specific person, on one specific day, on whatever device they have, and what to offer instead when something did not land. 
  • Own the measurement that makes it real. Weekly active learners is the number this role moves. There is a baseline. Setting the target with us, and owning the path to it, is part of the job. 
  • Treat mobile as a first class question rather than a port. Seven minutes attached to a real week is a phone experience far more often than a desk one. Whether that is a native client or something lighter is a genuine open decision with very different costs. 
  • Draw on a single library. Our own studio content, customer created content and content generated on the spot all sit together, and deciding what surfaces to whom is part of your job. 

This role is for you if you have 

  • A track record owning either a B2B2C product, where the buyer and the user are different people and the user did not choose you, or a consumer habit-formation product built to create usage rather than meet demand that already existed 
  • Evidence you have shipped personalisation, routing or recommendation work that measurably changed behaviour, and the scar tissue to know how often it does not 
  • Comfort on a platform that carries real history. You will build the new thing while the old thing earns the revenue, and sequencing that is part of the craft rather than an obstacle to it 
  • A habit of deciding. You gather input properly and then take the call, and you can say clearly what you are not doing and why 
  • A habit of working in the open. Drafts early, thinking visible, and you would rather be corrected on Tuesday than right on Friday 
  • A genuine interest in how people learn. You do not need a background in it, you do need to find it interesting, because you will work closely with people who have spent careers on it 
  • Comfort partnering with an embedded engineering manager on the team rather than managing engineers directly 

This role is not for you if 

  • You want a clean greenfield. That is a much easier engineering problem and a much worse bet, and it is not what this is 
  • You need the strategy finished before you start. It is being written now and you would be one of the people writing it 
  • You want to run the roadmap process. Product Operations owns that craft, this role owns the outcome 
  • You would rather own a feature area than a number 
  • You expect to set every priority yourself from day one. A leadership-set integration into the current platform is already on the roadmap when you arrive, yours to execute well, not to re-litigate

title: GTM Growth Manager
description:
Voice is becoming the primary interface for technology. For the first time in history, we can use natural language to control and interact with our devices, services, and applications, and we’re only at the beginning of the adoption of Voice and Physical AI across industries. Current voice interactions, however, still lack a fundamental human skill: nuanced understanding of audio scenes and environments. Navigating complex auditory scenes, distinguishing between multiple voices, or focusing on a main speaker are all part of the challenge of “teaching machines to hear like human beings.”

At ai-coustics, we’re building the audio intelligence layer and developer tooling to enable more robust and intelligent voice agents and Physical AI applications. Today, Voice AI companies like Perplexity, Retell, LiveKit or AssemblyAI use the ai-coustics SDK to prepare their agents for real-world acoustic challenges. Our models power thousands of agents worldwide and process millions of hours each month.

We are backed by leading early-stage investors including Connect Ventures, Partech, Inovia Capital, as well as angel investors from HuggingFace, DeepMind and Amazon with deep expertise in AI and developer infrastructure. These partners share our vision and are helping us build a world-class team operating with high levels of responsibility and velocity. We look for people who take ownership, think systemically, and want to solve challenging real-world problems in close collaboration with our customers. If you’re motivated by developing technology that is used in practice, shaping an emerging category and setting a new standard for how Voice AI works in the real world, you’ll feel at home at ai-coustics.

About the role

Developers find us, install the SDK, and start processing audio before we ever speak to them. Thousands of accounts have run audio through our models. Some become customers, but many sit somewhere between a first test and real production use. The opportunity is to identify the accounts with real potential, understand what moves them from testing to paying, and find what makes them grow from there.

You own that journey, from reaching promising developers and teams to converting and growing them. You use product and usage data to decide where to focus, get involved in promising evaluations early, and close startup and mid-market deals. You also experiment with outbound approaches to reach new prospects, identify ways to expand existing customers, and build and test the pricing and operational systems that make the whole motion work.

This isn't a conventional sales role or a RevOps role. It is a job for someone who wants to do both. If you only want to close, this will frustrate you. If you only want to analyse, you'll be uncomfortable when a number depends on you picking up the phone.

Tasks

  • Signup to paid — Carry the conversion number. Work out which trials are real, get into the evaluation early, cut time-to-value, and remove what's blocking the purchase.
  • Outbound — Own the motion end to end: target lists, sequencing, messaging, cadence, and the tooling. Run experiments and double down on what converts.
  • Full-cycle sales — Run startup and mid-market deals end to end: discovery, qualification, technical evaluation, pricing, negotiation, close.
  • Expansion and retention — Own NRR. Most start on one model and a fraction of their traffic. Find the next use case, catch the accounts going quiet before they churn, win back the ones that left.
  • Account intelligence — Build the scoring layer. Turn usage data into a ranked list, and keep the ICP current as the market moves.
  • Rev ops and reporting — Own HubSpot, the funnel model and the monthly numbers. You keep them accurate because we make decisions from them, and everyone from the board down reads the numbers you produce.
  • Pricing and packaging — Run experiments on the self-serve tiers: what's in each plan, where the limits sit, what triggers an upgrade. Ship, measure, roll out what lifts conversion.
  • AI-native operations — Build agents and automations across your whole role, pipeline generation to revenue operations. We already run this way and you'll extend it.
  • Voice of customer — Gather feedback from customer interactions so product knows what to build and marketing knows how to position.

Requirements

  • 2–5 years in a commercial role at a startup or scale-up, ideally with an AI, developer, API or infrastructure product, where you carried a number and personally owned part of a funnel. You've worked somewhere growing fast and know what it's like when the playbook doesn't exist yet, the targets move, and nobody hands you a territory.
  • You've closed. You can talk about specific deals you won and lost, and what you'd do differently.
  • Love data. You can build a funnel in a product analytics tool, interrogate a CRM, write a query to check a hunch, and spot when a number is lying to you. We use PostHog and HubSpot.
  • Experiment discipline. You can design a test, judge whether the result means anything, and say so when it doesn't.
  • Tool fluency. Claude Code, Codex, Lemlist, HubSpot, PostHog. You're fast on the stack and faster picking up what's next.
  • Comfortable with a technical buyer. You can follow a conversation about latency, benchmarks, SDK integration and model behaviour, ask useful questions, and know when to bring an engineer in.
  • You sell the way developers buy. Our customers evaluate before they talk to anyone and respond to evidence.
  • You use AI daily as an operational tool, not an experiment. You build workflows with it and have opinions about where it helps and where it produces noise.
  • Strong copywriting skills and written communication. You're able to A/B test copy and see what customers respond to.
  • High agency. You're joining a commercial team still being built, with no established playbook. Your instinct should be to go and find out rather than wait to be briefed.
  • Commercial generalist. You're comfortable wearing several hats in a day and don't wait for someone to define the lane.
  • Working language is English. German is useful and not required.
  • Bonus: you've worked in voice AI, speech or audio before. Not a requirement, but it will shorten your first month. Our customers are building voice agents and the vocabulary is specific. Caring about sound and how it works helps.

Benefits

  • Opportunity to work at a rapidly growing Voice AI startup, backed by top investors.
  • Compensation and equity: Competitive salary package, additional benefits and stock options, enabling you to take part in the company’s success.
  • Startup Culture: Dynamic, fast-paced environment with passionate and collaborative colleagues.
  • High Impact: Groundbreaking startup at a pivotal growth stage, making a real difference in how people experience audio.
  • Ownership & Autonomy: Take full ownership of projects and ship fast.
  • Work With the Best: World-class team of engineers and builders with ample room for professional growth.
  • Contribute to the Future: Define the landscape of Voice AI technology.

If you are ready to lead the charge in revolutionizing Voice AI and drive our startup to new heights, we would love to hear from you. Apply today to join the ai-coustics team!

title: Recruiter / Talent Acquisition Manager (all genders)

Wir suchen jemanden, der im Recruiting bereits angekommen ist - mit fundierter Praxis, einem klaren Verständnis für die Mechanik guter Prozesse und dem Ehrgeiz, den Bereich aktiv mitzuprägen. Du bewegst dich souverän zwischen operativer Exzellenz und strategischem Weitblick, zwischen Tempo und Präzision, zwischen Beratung und klarer Kante gegenüber Stakeholdern bis auf C-Level.

Recruiting bei uns ist kein ruhiges Gewässer. Es ist schnell, anspruchsvoll und ergebnisorientiert. Genau das soll dich reizen, nicht abschrecken.

Was du bewegst

Operative Verantwortung

  • End-to-End-Ownership vielfältiger Recruiting-Prozesse – unterschiedliche Funktionen, unterschiedliche Level, unterschiedliche Herausforderungen

  • Sparringspartner:in für Hiring Manager, Leadership und C-Level – von der Anforderungsschärfung bis zur finalen Entscheidung

  • Strukturierte, kompetenzbasierte Interviewführung mit hohem Anspruch an Qualität und Fairness

  • Aktive Marktbearbeitung durch gezieltes Sourcing

  • Eine Candidate Experience, die auch unter Zeitdruck überzeugt

Strategisches Ownership

  • Mitgestaltung des Talent-Acquisition-Bereichs in enger Abstimmung mit dem Head of - strukturell, prozessual, strategisch

  • Volle Verantwortung für den Recruiting-Funnel: Kennzahlen definieren, Conversion steigern, Engpässe erkennen, konsequent nachschärfen

  • Aufbau strategischer Talent Pools für Profile, die immer wieder gefragt sind

  • Entwicklung von Active-Search-Strategien

  • Verantwortung für Recruiting-Tools und -Systeme - von Auswahl bis Optimierung

  • Aufbau externer Partnerschaften, die unser Recruiting schlagkräftiger machen


DAS BRINGST DU MIT

  • Praktische Recruiting-Erfahrung, im Idealfall bereits über mehrere Funktionen und Senioritäten hinweg

  • Ein geschärftes Verständnis für strukturierte, datenbasierte Recruiting-Prozesse und Active Sourcing

  • Souveränität und Verhandlungsgeschick im Umgang mit anspruchsvollen Stakeholdern bis in die Geschäftsführung

  • Die Fähigkeit, gleichzeitig operativ tief einzusteigen und strategisch den Überblick zu behalten

  • Belastbarkeit und einen kühlen Kopf, wenn mehrere kritische Suchen parallel unter Druck stehen

  • Ein analytischer Blick auf Funnel, Kennzahlen und Prozessqualität

  • Verbindlichkeit, Beratungsstärke und den Mut, auch unbequeme Empfehlungen auszusprechen

  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse

Wir freuen uns auf deine Nachricht und helfen dir gerne weiter!

  • Office Foodji & Lunchit App: Immer bestens versorgt bei uns im Office oder Remote

  • bAV: Mit der Degura Pension Cloud sichern und bezuschussen wir jetzt schon deine Rente

  • Spendit Card: Wir stocken dein Gehalt auf! Mit Spendit stehen dir bis zu fünfzig Euro netto im Monat on top zur freien Verfügung

  • EGYM Wellpass: Mit uns bleibst du fit & wir bringen dich deutschlandweit in die angesagtesten Fitness- und Wellnessstudios

  • JobRad: Spring mit uns aufs Rad und lease dir dein Traumrad oder Pedelec

  • KITA/Kiga Kostenzuschuss: Wir bezuschussen deine Kosten für die Kinderbetreuung, damit deine Kinder immer bestens versorgt sind

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Du erhältst attraktive Promotions und Discounts verschiedener Brands

  • Food Tastings: Teste dich mit unserem Foodteam durch unsere Produkte und gestalte unser Sortiment von morgen

  • Development: Deine Weiterentwicklung liegt uns am Herzen und mit regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen und Trainings bieten wir dir spannende Entwicklungspfade – z. B. vom SDR zum Account Executive

  • Flexwork: Arbeite 30 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU Ausland

  • Top Office Lage: Genieße eine erstklassige Arbeitsumgebung im Münchener Glockenbachviertel mit der Isar vor der Tür

  • Team Events: Wir sind ein Team - beim Skiday, Frühstück, Culture Week oder Office Party feiern wir gemeinsam!

ÜBER UNS

Hi, schön, dass du da bist! Wir sind Foodji - ein Team aus Food-Lovern & Tech-Nerds.

Unsere Mission ist es, frisches, gesundes und vor allem leckeres Essen überall dort anzubieten, wo Menschen den Großteil ihres Alltags verbringen – in Büros, ganz gleich, ob im Gewerbegebiet oder mitten in der Stadt, während langer Schichten im Krankenhaus oder in den Tiefen einer Produktionshalle, in der rund um die Uhr Menschen arbeiten. Überall bieten wir vollwertige Gerichte, Snacks und Getränke genau dort an, wo und wann du sie brauchst.

Proprietäre Technologien, selbstlernende Algorithmen und effiziente Lieferketten helfen uns dabei, das Paradox zwischen frischem Essen, Verfügbarkeit und Nachhaltigkeit aufzulösen. Own the process that turns invoices into cash, and shape how trawa's Finance function scales with our customer base.

As our Accounts Receivable Accountant, you'll own the end-to-end AR and collections process. You'll be the person customers talk to when something on an invoice isn't clear, and the person internally who makes sure open items don't stay open. You'll work closely with Customer Success, Business Operations, and our Finance team.

If you're excited by ownership, an AI-first way of working, and building something that actually matters, this is your role.


What You'll Own

Collections and Dunning

  • Own the collections cadence end-to-end: monitor AR aging, prioritise the highest-impact accounts, and drive them to resolution via email and phone.

  • Manage our dunning process reliably and with the right tone: firm on cash, respectful of the customer relationshipDebitorenbuchhaltung und operative Prozesse.

Reconciliation and Cash Application

  • Reconcile incoming payments against open invoices, investigate and resolve unapplied cash, short-pays, and discrepancies.

  • Run structured reconciliations reliably, and independently drive ad-hoc analyses for complex payments or edge cases.

  • Support month-end close with AR reconciliations and clean aging reports.

Ticket Ownership and Customer Interaction

  • Take ownership of our AR ticket queue, which is currently high-volume and one of the most visible pain points across the company. You get on top of it, categorise what's coming in, and resolve the majority of tickets directly.

Who You Are

Must-haves

  • 3+ years of experience in Accounts Receivable, Collections, or Credit Control, or a comparable Finance role. Ideally in a high-volume and complex B2B environment

  • Solid understanding of AR processes: dunning, cash application, reconciliations, and month-end AR work.

  • Structured, analytical, and detail-oriented. You keep complex open items straight without losing the bigger picture.

  • Business fluent in English and solid written German (customer correspondence in German needs to work reliably). Spoken German is a strong plus but not required.

  • Comfortable in the standard office and analytics toolset (Excel or Google Sheets) and able to navigate independently.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with AI-powered reconciliation tools or modern ticketing systems.

  • Genuine curiosity for AI and automation. Bonus if you've already used Langdock, Claude, or similar tools to speed up your own work.

  • Experience in a fast-growing start-up or scale-up environment.


Your First 90 Days

  • Understand trawa's business model, customer base, and billing logic, including what makes energy billing genuinely complex

  • Map our AR process end-to-end (invoicing, collections, cash application, close) and get to know your key counterparts in Customer Success, BizOps, and Accounting

  • Take over recurring work: ticket triage, aging analysis, dunning follow-ups

Month 2: Take Ownership

  • You've shipped at least one meaningful process improvement and can point to its impact

  • You're actively shaping how our AR processes scale as trawa's customer base grows


Why trawa?

  • Direct collaboration with Finance leadership and cross-functional leaders from day one. Short paths, real decisions, real ownership

  • A uniquely complex business at the intersection of energy, software, and B2B operations. You'll learn a lot, fast

  • An AI-first and automation-first Finance team. You'll set up scalable processes and drive them forward through process automation and larger tool implementations.

  • Real room to grow as trawa scales, your scope grows with the company.

  • Flexible working, 30 vacation days, L&D budget, competitive compensation, VSOPs (share package), meal vouchers, Urban Sports Club membership, and a vibrant office culture in Berlin

Diversity at trawa

Everyone is welcome here. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace that values diversity, and we encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, physical or neurodiverse background.

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. We value ownership, learning speed, and aren't hunger over a perfect CV.

This is a company built for growth.

As Senior Technical Product Manager (f/m/x), this role isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger technical and business picture, working closely with Engineering, including how we use AI to move faster and cut down on repetitive work, and turning strategy into precise, technically grounded product decisions that create real value. Every change you ship affects millions of users, and that responsibility is what makes working at exmox exciting.

If you're energized by fast-moving markets, complex technical systems, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Own:

  • Technical product strategy & vision Together with Engineering leads, you shape the product vision, strategy, and roadmap with a clear understanding of technical constraints and opportunities. You define goals and success metrics, and continuously evolve product direction based on system capabilities, technical debt, and business priorities.

  • Discovery, scoping & prioritization You gather and balance inputs from engineering, user research, data, and stakeholders to deeply understand problems, including their technical complexity. You write detailed, unambiguous requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineers can act on immediately.

  • Agile ownership & delivery You own the product backlog end-to-end: grooming, refinement, sprint planning, and prioritization. You actively participate in technical discussions, architecture reviews, and sprint ceremonies, ensuring the team always has well-defined, ready-to-build work.

  • Technical stakeholder alignment You translate business needs into precise engineering requirements, and translate technical realities back into language stakeholders understand. You work closely with Engineering, UI/UX, Data, Marketing, and Operations to ensure alignment across the full product lifecycle.

  • Experimentation & continuous improvement You leverage A/B testing, analytics, and system monitoring to validate ideas, measure outcomes, and drive ongoing product and technical improvements. You understand data pipelines and instrumentation well enough to define the right metrics from the ground up.


What You Bring

  • Technical Product Manager experience Strong experience as a Technical Product Manager building digital products, ideally in mobile gaming, ad-tech, e-commerce, or online marketing. You've worked closely with engineering teams and are comfortable in technical conversations.

  • Engineering fluency You don't need to code, but you can read and discuss API contracts, system architectures, database schemas, and technical trade-offs. Engineers see you as a peer, not just a requirements writer.

  • Agile ownership You have deep hands-on experience owning a product backlog: writing epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria, running sprint ceremonies, and continuously improving team throughput and focus.

  • Data-driven product decisions Solid experience using quantitative data, A/B testing, funnel analysis, and product analytics tools to guide decisions. You understand how data is collected, structured, and interpreted, and can define instrumentation requirements yourself.

  • High-scale product teams At least 4 years of experience working with cross-functional engineering and product teams on high-scale digital products with millions of users.

  • Structured & organized Able to manage multiple workstreams, balance competing priorities, and deliver against realistic timelines without losing sight of the bigger picture


How We Win

  • Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.

  • Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.

  • See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.

title: Robot Learning Engineer
description:
Why this role is exciting

Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz, Knuspr.de, Kifli.hu, Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro, choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows.

We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match.

We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job.

You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them.

What you will own and deliver

  • The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong.

  • Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap.

  • The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows.

  • The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations.

  • Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after.

The scope

This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it.

What we are looking for

  • PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted.

  • You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall.

  • You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists.

  • Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim..

  • Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise.

  • AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was.

  • Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2.

What success looks like in 90 days

You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like.

Are we a good fit?

Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit?.

  • Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started

  • Benefits — see what we offer

Finance at Rohlik is being rebuilt to run on AI. We already have agents in production that chase overdue payments, process invoices, allocate cash and clear the team's inbox. The pieces work. What we need now is one person to own the whole thing and make it deliver at scale.

 

Role Overview

This is a new role that owns how AI and automation reshape the finance operating model across the Group. You will take a programme that is already live across procure to pay, order to cash and our shared services centre, and turn it from a set of promising experiments into the way finance actually runs.

You report to the Group CFO. You inherit a small team and a live roadmap, and you own the result. You decide what gets automated first, you build and ship with AI tools when that is the fastest way, and you hold every workstream to a number.

The role is deliberately hands on. You should be close enough to the work to build an agent or connect two systems through an API with AI assistance, even though you are not a software developer. You should also be senior enough to redesign how finance works and bring the rest of the business with you.

 

Why this role is exciting

  • You’ll inherit a live AI programme with real agents, real data and real impact from day one — not a greenfield slide deck.

  • You’ll shape how Finance actually runs across the Group as we move toward the next stage of growth — including the journey toward IPO readiness.

  • You’ll have access to a top-notch AI-first tech stack and the freedom to use it pragmatically.

  • You’ll work directly with the Group CFO, with fast decisions and no corporate red tape.

  • Your good ideas will be implemented almost immediately — not parked in a roadmap waiting for HQ approval.

  • You’ll lead a small team, but this is not a “manager from a distance” role. It’s highly hands-on, high-impact, and built for someone who wants to make things move fast.

 

What we expect from you

  • Own the AI and automation agenda across finance, from strategy through delivery to measured impact.

  • Lead process redesign the right way: map and understand the as-is, then design an agentic-first to-be rather than automating the old steps.

  • Lead complex cross-functional programmes across Finance, Tech and Operations, driving delivery through stakeholders and teams beyond your direct reporting line.

  • Bring the live programme to its targets, with a clear owner, baseline and deadline behind every workstream.

  • Redesign core finance processes around AI and agents, starting with close, reporting and forecasting.

  • Build and ship yourself when it is faster, using AI assisted tools to create agents and connect systems such as NetSuite, Rossum and n8n.

  • Lead and grow the team (three today) and raise AI fluency across finance and the SSC so the business can use what you build.

  • Track what matters and report it straight: automation rate, close time, cash allocation speed, cost and effort taken out.

  • Roll out across our five markets, balancing local reality against one Group standard.

 

What we look for

You have probably spent time in strategy consulting or in a transformation role, and you are now genuinely excited by what AI can do. You are a sharp generalist who can walk into a messy process, find the real problem, and fix it. You are as comfortable in a CFO pre-read as you are in the AI first tool building the thing.

  • A track record of leading transformation or automation programmes that actually delivered. A consulting, operations or generalist operator background all fit.

  • Strong understanding of finance processes, ideally gained through finance transformation, operating model redesign or automation programmes.

  • Hands on with AI. You can build agents and integrate APIs with AI assistance. You are not a software engineer and you do not need to be, but the tooling does not scare you.

  • You set baselines, name owners, hit deadlines, and say so early when something slips.

  • You can lead a small team and still do the work yourself.

  • You prioritise by impact and move fast. Better done than perfect.

  • You bring finance, tech and operations along with you.

  • Fluent in English. other languages will be an advantage.

  • Regular travel to Prague HQ required (min. 4 days per month)

What we offer

  • Unlimited vacation days to support a healthy work-life balance

  • Monthly vouchers: €45 tax-free via become.1

  • €20 monthly internet allowance

  • Knuspr Xtra account and 10% discount in the form of Knuspr credits / cashback

  • Great discounts through Corporate Benefits – fitness, travel, tickets, shopping and much more

  • Real growth: we’re not a traditional corporate.

  • Knuspr vibe: an international team, flat hierarchy, and a first-name culture where mistakes are seen as opportunities to learn

Local Operations Management (Wiesbaden)

Incident and Problem Management

  • Ensures incidents are logged, prioritised, diagnosed and resolved according to agreed procedures and service levels.

Change Management

  • Assesses changes for risk, impact, cost and resource requirements, and represents the location in Change Advisory Boards.
  • Ensures changes are planned, communicated, tested, implemented and reviewed in a controlled manner, minimizing disruption to operations.

Service Level Management

  • Negotiates service level requirements and agreed service levels with customers, and contributes to Service Level Agreements, Operational Level Agreements and underpinning contracts.

Cost, Resource and Vendor Management

  • Manages the operational and transition budget for the location, including cost planning, forecasting, tracking and variance reporting.
  • Provides inputs to customer budget processes, cost models and service rates, ensuring the full cost of operating transitioned services is identified and funded.
  • Identifies cost optimisation opportunities without compromising service levels or security.

title: Marketing Manager (m/f/d)
description:
MAOMAO is a fast-growing online supermarket for Asian food, combining e-commerce with content, community and social commerce.

We don't just sell products. We introduce people to new foods, brands, trends and cultures through TikTok, Instagram, livestreams, TikTok Shop, our online shop and our own products.

As MAOMAO continues to grow, we're looking for a Marketing Manager (m/f/d) who wants to take real ownership and help shape the next stage of our marketing.

Aufgaben

What You'll Do

Campaigns & Product Launches

You will plan and coordinate marketing campaigns, promotions, product launches and livestreams from idea to execution.

This includes:

  • developing campaign and launch plans
  • creating timelines, responsibilities and deadlines
  • coordinating content and communication across our channels
  • making sure everyone involved knows what needs to happen and when
  • keeping projects moving and following up on deliverables
  • identifying problems and dependencies early
  • reviewing results and turning learnings into better future campaigns

We are looking for someone who thinks beyond individual tasks and takes responsibility for making the overall project work.

TikTok Shop & Social Commerce

Social commerce is an important part of MAOMAO and an area we want to continue developing.

You will work on:

  • TikTok Shop campaigns and promotions
  • Seller Center and campaign management
  • livestream campaigns and activations
  • product and promotional planning
  • coordination with TikTok and external partners
  • identifying and testing new opportunities in social commerce

Experience with TikTok Shop is a plus, but not a requirement. Curiosity and the ability to learn quickly matter just as much.

Marketing & Content

You will work with our team to develop campaigns and content around Asian food, products, trends and culture.

You will help decide:

  • which products and topics we should focus on
  • how we communicate them to our audience
  • which content formats and channels make sense
  • how campaigns connect across TikTok, Instagram, our online shop, email and other channels

We want someone who doesn't just create marketing, but increasingly understands why something works and how we can make it better.

Team & Project Coordination

Good ideas only matter if they get executed.

You will help coordinate marketing projects across the team, keep track of priorities and deadlines and make sure projects move forward.

Depending on your experience, you may also:

  • coordinate responsibilities within the marketing team
  • improve workflows and processes
  • support and guide other team members
  • take responsibility for larger marketing initiatives
  • help shape marketing priorities together with the founders

There is room to take on more leadership responsibility as both you and MAOMAO grow.

Your Role Can Grow With You

We don't expect one person to be an expert in every area of marketing.

Depending on your experience, strengths and interests, you can gradually take on additional responsibility in areas such as:

Performance & KPIs
Analyzing campaign performance, defining measurable goals and using data to improve marketing decisions.

Marketing Budgets
Managing defined budgets and deciding how resources should be allocated across campaigns and channels.

CRM & Email Marketing
Developing how we communicate with existing customers and improve retention.

What Ownership Means at MAOMAO

Ownership is one of the most important parts of how we work.

It doesn't mean working endless hours or having all the answers.

It means thinking beyond the individual task.

If we are launching a new product in four weeks, we don't want someone who simply waits for a list of things to do.

We want someone who thinks:

What are we trying to achieve? What needs to happen? Which channels should we use? What content do we need? Who owns what? What are the deadlines? What are we missing? What could go wrong? And how will we know whether it worked?

Just as importantly, we value people who think in solutions, not only in problems.

Pointing out that something is not working is useful. But we expect you to go one step further:

What can we do about it? What are the options? What can we test now? What is the fastest reasonable next step?

You should be willing to make informed decisions, experiment, learn from results and iterate quickly rather than waiting for a perfect answer.

Not every idea will work. That is okay.

What matters is that we learn fast, adjust fast and keep moving.

The mindset we're looking for is:

“Here is the problem. Here are the options. Here is what I recommend we try next.”

Qualifikation

Who We're Looking For

We're open to candidates with different backgrounds and levels of experience, but we're looking for someone who has already gained meaningful hands-on marketing experience and is ready to take ownership.

You should:

  • have at least 2 years of relevant experience in marketing, e-commerce, social media, content, campaign management or a related field
  • have fluent German skills (C1 or native-level), as you will be developing marketing for a predominantly German-speaking audience
  • have strong working proficiency in English
  • be highly organized, reliable and proactive
  • take initiative and think ahead
  • be able to turn ideas into structured plans and execution
  • communicate clearly and follow through
  • feel comfortable taking responsibility for outcomes
  • think in solutions rather than simply escalating problems
  • be willing to experiment, test and iterate quickly
  • be comfortable making decisions even when not every answer is obvious
  • have a strong interest in e-commerce, social media and social commerce
  • be comfortable working with data, KPIs and budgets
  • enjoy working in a fast-moving environment
  • be hands-on when needed
  • learn quickly and actively look for ways to improve

Experience in e-commerce, TikTok, TikTok Shop, social media, CRM, performance marketing or campaign management is a plus.

Chinese language skills are a plus but they are NOT a requirement.

Benefits

Benefits

What we offer

  • A central marketing role with a high level of ownership and room to shape how we work
  • Direct collaboration with the founders
  • Founders with backgrounds in venture capital and e-commerce
  • An existing marketing and content team to work with
  • Our own office, warehouse and content setup in Berlin
  • Short decision-making paths and the freedom to actually implement ideas
  • Plenty of room to experiment, test new formats and iterate quickly
  • The opportunity to work at the intersection of e-commerce, social media, TikTok Shop, livestreaming and brand building
  • The opportunity to shape campaigns and launches from idea to execution instead of owning only one small part of the process
  • Clear professional and personal development opportunities, including the potential to take on more leadership responsibility
  • A young, international team with a lot of passion and team spirit
  • Employee discount across our assortment

Interested?

Send us your CV and a short introduction telling us why you want to join MAOMAO and what excites you about this role.

We'd also like you to answer one question:

Tell us about a marketing campaign, project or experiment you took ownership of. What was your goal, what did you do, and what was the result?

It doesn't have to be a huge campaign or a perfect success. We're interested in how you think, how you approach problems and what you learn from the things you try.

One last thing: We don't mind if you use AI to help with your application – we use AI too. But if your application could be sent to 50 other companies by simply replacing the company name, it's probably not for us. Show us why MAOMAO, and show us how you think.

If you want to take ownership, move fast and help us grow a category that has been treated as a niche for far too long, we'd love to hear from you.

Maybe you're the Sriracha to our noodle soup. 🌶️🍜

title: Lead Implementation & Delivery (f/m/d)
description:
We're looking for an experienced implementation, delivery or technical operations lead to own delivery after a contract is signed — and to play a central role in working out what actually makes our product work for customers.

This one is for you if:

  • You'd rather build the playbook than wait for one to exist
  • You get real satisfaction from being the person people can count on — customers and colleagues alike
  • Making a genuinely complex, technical product work in the real world, on a factory floor and not just a slide deck, sounds like a good problem to have

Every factory should be as easy to redesign as a CAD file. RIIICO scans real production floors and turns the raw point cloud into a structured, living model of the plant — machines, robots and infrastructure recognised by AI, matched to CAD, usable directly in the engineering tools our customers already run. Line changes that used to take months of manual work now take days.

We're seed-funded, backed by Earlybird, PiLabs and seed + speed, with angels including Joe Kaeser, former CEO of Siemens.

Team: two application engineers report to you directly, and you steer our data delivery team, which has its own manager and five people.
Start: as soon as you can.

Tasks

You'll own the entire post-sale delivery, from signed deal to a customer who's live, confident and getting real value. Our customers are enterprise manufacturers, so the accounts you own are complex and technically demanding from day one. As an early hire there's no existing playbook — expect to blend hands-on implementation, delivery operations and testing product-market-fit hypotheses directly with customers.

  • Own the post-sale journey, from handover through to stable, value-delivering adoption
  • Build the adoption framework for enterprise accounts, and define what "first value" means
  • Keep a current view of every account: check-ins, early risk signals, retention plans
  • Handle escalations yourself, at both operational and management level
  • Own the Sales-to-delivery handover and keep capacity visible and realistic
  • Develop the lightweight processes that make delivery repeatable as patterns emerge
  • Lead and develop your team, and shape how Delivery is structured as we grow
  • Test the product-market-fit hypotheses Sales brings back, and feed findings into Product and Go-To-Market

What this looks like in your first six months:

  • Months 1–2 — run two live enterprise implementations yourself, end to end, so you know where the product and the process actually break
  • Months 2–3 — take over the Sales-to-delivery handover and make capacity visible enough that Sales doesn't promise what delivery can't back up
  • Months 3–4 — define what "first value" means for an enterprise account, and the timeframe we hold ourselves to
  • Months 4–6 — turn what you've learned into the first delivery playbook, and bring at least two validated product-market-fit findings back to Product and Sales

Requirements

  • 4–6 years in technical implementation, delivery, project lead or technical operations roles, at a B2B company serving manufacturing or industrial customers
  • Experience as an early hire building implementation or delivery processes from scratch in a startup or scale-up
  • Experience owning the interface between Sales and a technical delivery team: handover, capacity oversight, and escalations you resolved independently
  • Enough technical depth to get fluent fast in discrete manufacturing, factory planning or industrial automation. You don't need to have done this exact thing before, but you do need to hold a credible conversation with a manufacturing engineer within a few months
  • Fluent written and spoken German and English. We work in English internally; customer work happens in German

You're eligible to work in Germany — EU/EEA citizenship, or an existing work or residence permit. We aren't able to sponsor visas for this role.

You'll fit if:

  • You're decisive and comfortable holding your ground when Sales pushes on scope or timeline — and just as good at negotiating a pragmatic trade-off without compromising commitments already made
  • You're pragmatic and action-first: you build the process as the pattern emerges, rather than designing the system before you understand the reality
  • You have commercial instinct: you notice what's working and bring it to Sales as an expansion opportunity
  • You're a fast learner with strong situational awareness, equally comfortable on a shop floor and in front of a senior stakeholder

  • 30 days' holiday
  • Deutschlandticket
  • Based in our Düsseldorf office, with the flexibility to work from home
  • Regular customer site visits — a genuine mix of factory floor and desk, not travel every week
  • Real ownership from day one, with a direct line to founders and leadership on decisions that matter
  • The chance to define what this function becomes as we grow
  • A diverse, international team

Apply with your CV — no cover letter needed.

  1. Short intro call — 30 minutes

The written questions are how we get to know how you think before anyone sits in a room. They're the reason we don't ask for a cover letter.

title: Brand & Product Marketing
description:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP.

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

Why this role is a blank canvas

Brand is the one asset that compounds while everything else at a startup resets. Every deck, every customer story, every post builds on the last one, and the person who builds that foundation owns something no later hire can claim.

You will be one of the first people on our GTM team and the first owner of how Atira looks, sounds, and gets found: our positioning, our visual identity, our customer stories, and our presence in a market where no one has built a great brand yet. You work directly with the founders, who stay hands-on with positioning while you turn it into something the whole company builds on. And you won't start from zero: you'll build on our recently completed rebranding with a top-tier design agency and turn the new identity into everything Atira ships.

You won't be someone who "supports marketing" at Atira. You'll build a company's brand from scratch in one of the hardest, most valuable B2B markets there is.

How the role sits in the team

You are the first person at Atira whose full-time job is brand and marketing. You will define how Atira presents itself to the public, both from a strategic and operational perspective. The role sits at the heart of our GTM team with our BDR, AE, and GTM Engineer, and you work across every department: sales needs decks and stories, engineering needs a tech blog, product needs launches told in buyer language, recruiting needs an employer brand. You are the connective tissue that makes all of it look and sound like one company.

What you will do

You will shape how Atira presents itself to the public, across every medium: text, visuals, web, fairs, and events. Concretely:

  • Build the messaging foundation. Together with the founders, constantly refine who Atira is for, what we claim, and why we win

  • Own the visual identity. Consistent design across website, decks, product touchpoints, and events. You own the design system and the rules it is built upon

  • Make Atira visible. LinkedIn presence, customer stories, industry fairs and events. The goal is measurable: inbound interest and recognition among our target buyers and recruiting prospects

  • Grow into product marketing. Once the foundation stands, translate product capability into buyer language: launch narratives, one-pagers, demo storylines, side by side with our engineers and FDEs

What we are looking for

Creativity, hunger, structure, and the kind of taste that makes Atira iconic. We care more about who you are than about your CV. We have hired strong people from non-traditional backgrounds before and will confidently do it again.

That said, here is what we typically see in strong candidates:

  • Trained in a high-performing environment. 2+ years as part of a larger marketing or brand team, or under a strong marketing lead, at a startup, scaleup, or agency. You learned the craft from experienced people before owning it alone

  • Ownership evidence. You have owned a brand-shaped project end to end: rebuilt a startup's messaging and deck, ran a rebrand or website relaunch, or built a founder's LinkedIn presence to real reach

  • Craft. Your portfolio shows crisp writing and strong visual judgment. At Atira we highly value people who have clear opinions and are not afraid to share them!

  • Complex B2B exposure. Experience with, or demonstrated affinity for, technical or industrial B2B. You can talk to engineers and buyers without losing them

  • Self-directed. Comfortable owning the function alone, setting your own priorities, and shipping without a team

  • German + English. Fluent German for DACH industrial buyers and events, excellent English for global content

What you'll get

  • Real ownership. You are the first brand hire and build the function from zero. The brand Atira carries into the next hundred hires is the one you built

  • Direct line to the founders. You work hands-on with them on positioning and turn founder knowledge into public presence

  • Validated traction to work with. Leading industrial customers, several with revenues above €1B, and real stories waiting to be told

  • A rebrand to build on. Fully redesigned branding guidelines from our recently completed rebranding exercise with a top-tier brand agency, ready for you to roll out and evolve

  • Competitive salary & equity package and additional benefits including Wellpass, JobRad and company dinners.

  • Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity.

What success looks like after a few months

  • Atira has a positioning and messaging foundation adopted company-wide, a deck and template system every team actually uses, and a refreshed look that reflects it

  • Target buyers recognize us: growing LinkedIn engagement from ICP accounts, 2-3 published customer stories, presence at a key industry event, and the first inbound leads traceable to your work

  • The content engine runs without founder prompting, and brand requests from sales and recruiting get handled with fast turnaround

  • Purposeful work – your role will have a positive impact on patients, their families, and healthcare professionals.

  • Company culture – we believe in flat hierarchies that promote high performance and strong team dynamics. We foster an environment characterized by mutual respect, loyalty, and recognition. Together, we strive for our goals – and expect the same from you.

In this role, you can make an impact and grow with us as Tech Lead (Agent Frontend) (m/w/d):

You will take end-to-end technical ownership of the Recare Agent – our AI-native interface that orchestrates capabilities like Voice and Extract+Docs into reliable, compliant workflows for hospital environments. This is a highly visible product area where engineering decisions directly define user experience, reliability, and trust in AI-driven healthcare workflows.

  • You own the technical direction of the Recare Agent – from architecture decisions to roadmap execution and delivery predictability.

  • You lead the team as the technical backbone and escalation point, ensuring clarity, speed, and quality in execution.

  • You design and evolve the agent architecture, especially around agentic UI patterns and orchestration logic.

  • You enable the team through hands-on mentorship, code reviews, and removing blockers fast.

  • You drive reliability, performance, observability, and security across all agent workflows in a highly sensitive healthcare context.

  • You build and ship frontend systems using React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on scalable, maintainable architecture.

  • You collaborate closely with Product, Design, and QA to sharpen scope, manage trade-offs, and ensure predictable delivery.

  • You ensure production readiness through clear runbooks, stable releases, and measurable SLAs.

How we build:

We use a modern frontend stack to build and ship a highly interactive, AI-powered agent experience that must be fast, reliable, and safe in production healthcare environments.

  • React and TypeScript

  • Apollo (GraphQL proxy layer; REST-based backend services)

  • HeroUI with styled-components

  • Storybook (component-driven development)

  • Webpack 5 (with parts gradually migrating to Vite / SWC)

  • CircleCI (Jest, Cypress, visual regression testing)

  • SonarCloud (code quality & security analysis)


Here’s how we picture you as our Tech Lead (Agent Frontend) (m/w/d):

  • You bring 6+ years of professional software development experience and have led and owned technical directions team outcomes end to end.

  • You have strong expertise in TypeScript and React and are confident building complex, stateful UIs with asynchronous or streaming-driven interactions.

  • You understand how to design, ship, and evolve frontend systems in a production environment with a strong focus on quality and maintainability.

  • You bring solid foundations in CI/CD and testing frameworks (e.g. Jest, Cypress) and a clear interest in deeper engineering topics such as pipelines, caching strategies, and performance optimization.

  • You think in systems and trade-offs, and you actively drive for simple, scalable architectures while maintaining a high bar for engineering quality.

  • You take ownership naturally – you act as a reliable escalation point, ensure clarity in execution, and help the team stay unblocked and focused.

  • You communicate clearly and effectively in a remote-first environment, with strong collaboration skills across Product, Design, and QA.

  • You care about security and privacy by design and are comfortable working in a healthcare context where reliability, compliance, and trust are critical.

  • You communicate confidently in English and are comfortable operating in an international environment.

title: Werkstudent EV Sales & Deal Operations (m/w/d)
description:

Werde Teil von Aampere, einem Seed-Stage VC-backed Startup, das den europäischen Markt für gebrauchte E-Autos neu definiert. Der Markt ist fragmentiert, intransparent und schwer vertrauenswürdig, deshalb bauen wir die Infrastruktur, die das ändert, damit mehr Elektroautos ein zweites Leben bekommen und der Wandel zur Elektromobilität wirklich an Fahrt aufnimmt.

Unser Team kommt aus der deutschen Startup-Szene und der Automobilwelt, mit Erfahrung bei Autarc, Limehome, Cardino, Wemolo, Alasco, Porsche, Mercedes und KPMG.

Die Stelle ist ab sofort zu besetzen. Wenn du etwas bewegen möchtest, dann werde Teil unseres Teams.


Deine Mission

Du hast Lust auf direkten Kundenkontakt, gehst gerne auf Menschen zu und Autos sind für dich nicht einfach nur Fortbewegungsmittel, sondern ein echtes Interesse? Dann bist du bei uns im Sales Team genau richtig.

Startup-Alltag: Du bringst dich dort ein, wo du gebraucht wirst, mit deinen individuellen Stärken und Interessen.


Das bringst du mit

Dein Background: Du bist aktuell immatrikuliert im Bachelor- oder Masterstudium. Dein Studiengang ist für uns zweitrangig, viel wichtiger sind deine strukturierte Arbeitsweise und dein Blick für saubere Prozesse.
Kommunikationsstärke: Du gehst offen auf Menschen zu, telefonierst gerne und fühlst dich im direkten Kundenkontakt wohl.
Interesse an Autos: Kein Muss, aber definitiv ein Plus, denn du wirst viel mit Fahrzeugdaten arbeiten.
Entrepreneurial Mindset: Du hast Lust auf ein Umfeld, in dem sich Dinge schnell bewegen, zeigst Eigeninitiative und willst aktiv mitgestalten statt nur Dienst nach Vorschrift zu leisten.
Verfügbarkeit: Du hast 20 Stunden pro Woche Zeit für uns, in den Semesterferien gerne mehr.
Sprachkenntnisse: Du beherrschst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2) und Englisch sicher in Wort und Schrift.


Why Aampere?

Wachstum & Ownership: Du bekommst vom ersten Tag an echte Verantwortung, triffst eigene Entscheidungen und wirst als vollwertiges Teammitglied behandelt: im schnelllebigen Umfeld kannst du entsprechend schnell aufsteigen. Student steht auf dem Vertrag, nicht auf deiner Rolle.
Urban Sports Club oder Job Ticket: healthy team, happy team
Late Dinner im Office: Wenn es abends länger wird, übernehmen wir dein Dinner (Uber Eats)
Offsite: bis jetzt waren wir am Lago Maggiore, in den Alpen und am Tegernsee, what's next?

title: Senior Fullstack Developer – Business Automation (m/w/d)

Softwareentwicklung

  • Entwicklung TypeScript-basierter Automatisierungen und Services entlang unserer gesamten Wertschöpfungskette im HubSpot CRM

API- & Event-getriebene Architektur

  • Einsatz der HubSpot CRM APIs für Objekte, Assoziationen und Batch-Operationen

description:
Du hast schon mal etwas mit KI gebaut, das danach wirklich jemand benutzt hat, und willst nicht wieder ein Praktikum, in dem du Folien formatierst?

Dann lies weiter.

Aufgaben

Was du hier machst

Immotalente besetzt kaufmännische Stellen in Hausverwaltungen. Dahinter läuft ein selbstgebautes System: Kandidaten werden gefunden, bewertet und angeschrieben, über sechzehn Mandate hinweg. Dazu ein Wissensspeicher, in dem Mandate, Kunden und Abläufe liegen und aus dem heraus KI-Agenten arbeiten.

Das System funktioniert, und es hat Lücken. Du arbeitest an beidem.

Du baust Agenten für Aufgaben, die heute Handarbeit sind. Interviewnotizen zu Kandidatendossiers. Kundebriefings zu Mandatsakten. Prüfläufe, die melden, wenn eine Tabelle still aufgehört hat zu rechnen. Terminvorschläge, Nachfassen, Berichte.

Du entwickelst die Textqualität weiter. Die Ansprachetexte an Kandidaten klingen noch nach Maschine. Woran das liegt, ist analysiert und dokumentiert. Es umzusetzen ist offen, und es ist die Arbeit mit dem größten Hebel.

Du schließt Lücken im Bestand. Echte Fahrzeiten statt geschätzter. Datenprüfungen vor dem Import. Ein Abnahme-Test, der vor jeder Freigabe läuft.

Und du prüfst, was du gebaut hast. In diesem System sind Fehler unsichtbar: eine Spalte hat fünf Wochen nichts gerechnet, während die Oberfläche „100 Prozent fertig" anzeigte. Wer hier baut, ohne hinterher das Verhalten zu prüfen, richtet mehr Schaden an als Nutzen. Das ist die eine Regel, die nicht verhandelbar ist.

Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Gründer. Keine Ebene dazwischen, keine Abstimmungsrunden.

Qualifikation

Was du mitbringst

Du hast schon etwas gebaut, das funktioniert hat. Ein Skript, ein Automatisierungs-Workflow, ein Werkzeug mit einer KI dahinter, irgendetwas, das ein Problem gelöst hat, das nicht deins war. Zeig es uns, das zählt mehr als jede Note.

Zusammen mit Claude & Co kommst du mit JSON und einer REST-Schnittstelle klar und schreibst kleine Skripte, in JavaScript oder Python. Du schreibst sauberes Deutsch und merkst, wenn ein Satz nach Maschine klingt. Du hast die Angewohnheit, nach einer Änderung nachzusehen, ob sie wirklich umgesetzt wurde, statt der Erfolgsmeldung zu glauben.

Welches Fach du studierst, ist zweitrangig. Immobilien- oder Recruiting-Vorkenntnisse brauchst du nicht. Sie sind hilfreich, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Benefits

Was du davon hast

  • Du baust für einen echten Betrieb, nicht für eine Übungsaufgabe. Was du baust, läuft am nächsten Tag gegen echte Kandidaten und echte Kunden.
  • Du arbeitest mit dem aktuellen Werkzeugkasten: Claude, Clay, n8n, Lemlist, Recruiterflow, eigene HTML-Werkzeuge. Nichts davon ist Spielzeug, alles davon ist im Einsatz.
  • Du siehst die ganze Kette, von der Suche über die Bewertung bis zur Platzierung. Die meisten Praktika zeigen dir einen Ausschnitt.
  • Du bekommst ein Zeugnis mit Zahlen darin, nicht mit Aufgabenlisten. Was du gebaut hast, was es eingespart hat, was du gefunden hast.

Wie es weitergeht

Melde dich über diese Anzeige. Erzähle von dir und wann dein Praktikum starten muss, wie lange es geht, und ein Link oder Screenshot von etwas, das du gebaut hast. Zwei Sätze dazu, was daran schwierig war.

Wir antworten innerhalb von drei Werktagen.
